tb21_profile.skill: Read a program in an unfamiliar legacy language (COBOL record layouts, PIC/level-01 fields, sequential .DAT file I/O) and re-implement its semantics in Python so the mutated data files come out byte-identical
tb21_profile.domain: GnuCOBOL 3 / mainframe-style fixed-format flat-file batch processing (accounts, books, transactions .DAT records) re-hosted on Python
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec by cross-language port, verified differentially against the reference implementation's output

verifier_notes: software-engineering_20260419_065313_005 is graded `weak` (1/11 substantive) but its test_output_matches_awk actually shells out to gawk on the reference script and diffs the Python output line by line - that is the same differential check cobol-modernization itself uses, so the grade badly understates it; I treat it as strong. software-engineering_20260606_172606_005 is graded FREE and the grade is wrong: tests/test_outputs.py runs the C binary and moviedb.py on the same command stream and compares every field of the resulting binary DB (asserts live inside a run_and_compare helper, which the regex heuristic misses). Because the FREE rule is checked mechanically I kept it out of final_top10 anyway; it is the single best-shaped CalibForge candidate after the AWK one and a merge step that can re-grade should promote it. tw_12315 (FREE) is the only TerminalWorld candidate with real cross-language-format skill; kept in per_source, barred from final.

notes: CalibForge is decisively the best pool for this task and the only one containing real COBOL material (copybooks, EBCDIC cp500, COMP-3): the v1 pool has zero COBOL hits under `tools.py search all "COBOL|GnuCOBOL|cobc "`. Terminal-Lego-15k is the weakest corpus here - it is StackOverflow-derived and has no port-a-legacy-program tasks at all; ranks 4-10 there are fixed-width formatting and binary-record fragments and none deserve above overall 3. TerminalWorld is nearly as thin: only tw_241070 and tw_12315 are defensible, and tw_12315 is FREE. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has nothing verified (all `absent`) but its Elixir escript family is a genuine behaviour-preserving port genre that retrieval never surfaced; the shortlist for RTS was entirely compute_gcd/fstab boilerplate. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench lose on task_form as expected, but Rebench's axelrod (Python-must-match-Fortran) and pyccel (Python-to-Fortran/C transpiler) clusters are a much better answer than anything retrieval returned for that corpus. Merge step: rank 1 and the CalibForge moviedb task (kept out of final_top10 only because of the mechanical FREE rule) are both near-duplicates of this TB2.1 task's template; if only one port-template task can be taken, take rank 1.
